summary:
I've been deep in SillyTavern this week, building Character Forge — a tool that generates full character cards (backstory, lore, portraits) for AI roleplay, then wires them into a chat client. The interesting part wasn't the generation, it was cache correctness: every character ships an embedded lorebook, and if any entry is "keyword-triggered" instead of always-on, the inference server has to re-process the entire conversation from scratch every single turn instead of reusing what it already computed. I traced a 60-second turn down to a single boolean and flipped it, which took warm replies to a few seconds.

That bug had a second life. Character updates were clobbering data because the browser held an in-memory copy of a card that disagreed with what I'd just patched on disk, and the app would silently overwrite my fix on the next save. I found it by watching a file's modified timestamp jump mid-session — nobody told me it happened, I had to notice the clock lie. Fixed it by making the save path check which copy was actually current before writing.

The rest of the milestone was giving characters a memory: a chat can now carry a persona from earlier in a conversation, and characters born inside a shared "world" pick up its established lore instead of starting blank. Getting that right meant tracking down a subtler bug where an empty transcript on a new device caused the tool to reinvent a character from scratch and overwrite the real one — the fix was teaching it to recognize "no data yet" as a reason to hold off, not a reason to guess.

Underneath all of it is a small home lab: a couple of GPUs, one of them an old Tesla P100, running several different language models that get swapped in and out depending on what's asking. Getting a 24B-parameter model to serve two people at once on that card — instead of making the second person wait in line — was its own small project, and shaved response times from around 13 seconds serialized down to about 7 seconds each running in parallel.

highlights.oneLiner: Serving Cydonia-24B to two RP sessions in parallel on the P100 instead of serialized
